section_summary: This section covers fertilizer and chemical production, aluminum policy, and a U.S. Army vehicle rebuilding program in occupied Japan. Later documents report on chemical plant efficiency and reparations, production of wire, cellulose and electrical equipment, and prospects for industrial recovery in 1950. Several items are record sheets, corrections, drafts, enclosures or press clippings filed with the substantive correspondence.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement sheet for Tokyo telegram
subfiles.about: Designates a replacement record copy for a missing action copy.
subfiles.summary: The replacement copy is to be returned to Central Records for filing.

subfiles.title: Angaur phosphate project and British criticism
subfiles.to: Department of War; Secretary of State
subfiles.about: SCAP defends phosphate mining on Angaur for Japan's fertilizer needs and objects to British criticism.
subfiles.summary: SCAP says the project began with Combined Food Board authorization and later used Japanese labor under U.S. control, with Japan meeting the expenses. The message argues that British public criticism harms Allied solidarity and asks the Department to consider representations in London.

subfiles.title: Correction to Tokyo telegram number
subfiles.about: Corrects the serial number of the June 28 Tokyo message.
subfiles.summary: The message number C-53689 should read 173.

subfiles.title: Charge slip
subfiles.about: Records a file charge against a document.
subfiles.summary: Charge form cites file 893.659/6-2247.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about Japanese lace and net machines
subfiles.about: Requests counts of intact Levers, curtain and plain net machines in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Nottingham Chamber of Commerce requested the information.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Swanson's fertilizer articles
subfiles.about: Thanks Swanson for articles concerning Japanese fertilizers and soil survey work.
subfiles.summary: Whitman says the papers interest officials working on Japan's serious food situation.

subfiles.title: Army position on aluminum production in Japan
subfiles.about: Discusses proposed alumina imports, Japanese aluminum production and safeguards for reparations removals.
subfiles.summary: Draper reports no completed SCAP proposal arising from talks with Reynolds and Permanente. The Army awaits SCAP's response on proposed 1948 ingot production and wants contracts to avoid delaying removal of aluminum capacity designated for reparations.

subfiles.title: Routing slip for agreed cables
subfiles.about: Forwards copies of cables agreed with Bowman on March 17.
subfiles.summary: Routing note accompanies the agreed cable texts.

subfiles.title: Fragment on Netherlands East Indies bauxite offer
subfiles.about: Describes proposed bauxite sales to Japan and possible payment terms.
subfiles.summary: NEI representatives offer at least 50,000 tons annually and seek prompt negotiations.

subfiles.title: Draft cable on Japanese aluminum production
subfiles.about: Sets conditions for aluminum production serving Japanese needs and exports.
subfiles.summary: The draft calls for justification under occupation directives, protection of reparations removals and advance notice of export arrangements.

subfiles.title: Cable to SCAP on aluminum and bauxite
subfiles.about: Transmits the aluminum policy conditions, Netherlands East Indies bauxite offer and supporting background.
subfiles.summary: The cable accepts the proposed production program if occupation needs are justified and reparations are not delayed. It seeks advance notice of export arrangements and describes possible NEI bauxite terms. A following note explains the interdepartmental agreement and cites the occupation directive.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Swanson fertilizer paper
subfiles.about: Thanks Swanson for a paper on fertilizer practices for Japanese staple crops.
subfiles.summary: Whitman says the paper and maps will aid Far Eastern research.

subfiles.title: Eighth Army vehicle rebuilding operation in Japan
subfiles.about: Reports U. Alexis Johnson's inspection of the Eighth Army's Big-5 vehicle rebuilding program.
subfiles.summary: The despatch describes four plants rebuilding engines, vehicles, tires and sedans with American civilian supervisors and about 16,000 Japanese workers. It gives planned capacities, explains the use of Pacific stockpiles and Japanese subcontractors, and observes that the Tokyo engine plant could readily support new manufacture.

subfiles.title: Internal note on O'Leary memorandum
subfiles.about: Introduces O'Leary's account of wasteful Japanese chemical production.
subfiles.summary: The note links the problem to subsidy, allocation and exchange-rate reforms.

subfiles.title: Handwritten marginal note
subfiles.about: Contains a partly illegible comment on the preceding memorandum.
subfiles.summary: Most of the handwritten text is unreadable.

subfiles.title: Army transmittal of O'Leary memorandum
subfiles.about: Forwards O'Leary's memorandum at Joseph Dodge's request.
subfiles.summary: Porter encloses the memorandum on soda ash and caustic soda.

subfiles.title: Signed copy of Army transmittal
subfiles.about: Duplicates the letter forwarding O'Leary's memorandum.
subfiles.summary: Signed copy of Porter's March 16 transmittal.

subfiles.title: Present Uneconomical Production of Soda Ash and Caustic Soda
subfiles.about: Argues that scarce coal and salt should be concentrated in fewer Japanese Solvay-process plants.
subfiles.summary: O'Leary estimates that operating two plants instead of three would lower costs without reducing output. He treats the case as typical of inefficient allocations and subsidized production in Japan.

subfiles.title: Butterworth reply to Dodge
subfiles.about: Thanks Dodge for O'Leary's memorandum and comments on industrial rationalization.
subfiles.summary: Butterworth supports reducing wasteful production, subsidies and distorted exchange rates. He also warns that dismissals associated with plant consolidation will require expanded unemployment relief.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement sheet for ferrotungsten telegram
subfiles.about: Designates a replacement record copy for a missing Tokyo telegram action copy.
subfiles.summary: The replacement is to be returned for filing.

subfiles.title: Ferrotungsten available for export
subfiles.to: Secretary of State and U.S. supply agencies
subfiles.about: Seeks markets and price advice for Japanese ferrotungsten exports.
subfiles.summary: SCAP reports about 900 tons available and notes rejected sales whose ultimate destinations included Poland and Austria.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Pope chemical plant report
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a SCAP release on Frederick Pope's chemical industry survey and a related Newsweek article.
subfiles.summary: The despatch summarizes Pope's recommendations on management, loans, reparations, fertilizer chemicals and industrial advice.

subfiles.title: SCAP release and Pope report on Japanese chemical plants
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers; public
subfiles.about: Surveys 42 Japanese chemical plants and recommends measures to improve production and recovery.
subfiles.summary: Pope identifies weak management, scarce capital and materials, high costs and disruptive reparations plans. He recommends loans, improved fuel and fertilizer inputs, protection of useful plants, foreign technical exchange and a temporary engineering board. The SCAP introduction reports a substantial rise in chemical output since 1945 and revised deconcentration decisions.

subfiles.title: What's Wrong in Japan? Plenty, Blasts Survey
subfiles.about: Reports Frederick Pope's criticism of Japanese chemical industry policy and occupation decisions.
subfiles.summary: The article emphasizes Pope's calls for experienced managers and loans to industry. It quotes his objections to chemical-plant reparations, deconcentration and decisions based on unreliable production figures.

subfiles.title: Japanese cellulose production figures
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards SCAP figures for Japanese cellulose-related plants, production and imports.
subfiles.summary: The figures cover cellulose nitrate, acetate, cellophane and films.

subfiles.title: Information on Japanese woven wire industry
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports factory, machinery, workforce, output and export figures for woven wire.
subfiles.summary: SCAP data describe 79 factories and compare 1947–48 production and exports.

subfiles.title: Japanese manufacture of picric acid and chloropicrin
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards an Australian technical inquiry and SCAP's account of Japanese production processes.
subfiles.summary: SCAP says chloropicrin is being made from surplus picric acid and describes former picric-acid methods and reaction vessels used by several Japanese companies. A corrected technical paragraph is included.

subfiles.title: Statistics covering production of electric equipment
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits monthly Japanese electrical equipment production statistics.
subfiles.summary: The enclosed table covers 1948 and January–September 1949.

subfiles.title: Monthly electrical equipment production table
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Lists monthly output of motors, transformers, instruments, batteries, wire, cable and bulbs.
subfiles.summary: Table reports monthly production for 1948 and January–September 1949.

subfiles.title: Ammonium chloride plant inquiry for India
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards SCAP's answer to India's inquiry about Japanese ammonium chloride producers and plant equipment.
subfiles.summary: SCAP finds no current commercial ammonium chloride production in Japan but identifies firms able to propose a new plant. It gives provisional estimates for Gledd and Solvay process installations, subject to site and utility details.

subfiles.title: Fall fertilizer distribution in Japan
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a SCAP release comparing fall 1949 fertilizer deliveries with 1948.
subfiles.summary: Reported deliveries of nitrogenous fertilizer, superphosphate and potash rose over the prior year, with wide differences among prefectures. Shortage of farm funds and rain delayed some purchases and planting.

subfiles.title: Pearl finish on buttons and beads
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards SCAP's description of Japanese imitation-pearl coating methods.
subfiles.summary: The note describes hand dipping glass beads and buttons in pearlized lacquer, repeated coatings and materials required for imitation-pearl production.

subfiles.title: Chemical and industrial forecast for 1950
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits a SCAP bulletin forecasting Japanese chemical and industrial production in 1950.
subfiles.summary: The despatch attributes an optimistic forecast to SCAP's Industry Division chief. It anticipates more chemical fertilizer, soda products, synthetic dyes, cellulose acetate products, industrial oils and other goods, supported by improved coal and power supplies, trade arrangements and industrial efficiency.
